S.FORM: sua tia=kari=maku masini-a ia, tia=ku pu-isua sua ni-pala-anal-a naparamaci miana.
S.PHON: sua tiakarimaku maʂinia ia tiaku puisua sua nipaɾaanaɾa naparamatʂi miana
S.FORM: sua tiakarimaku masinia ia, tiaku puisua sua niparaanara naparamaci miana.
S.PHON: sua tiaka[r|ɾ]imaku maʂinia ia tiaku puisua sua nipa[r|ɾ]aana[r|ɾ]a napa[r|ɾ]amatʂi miana
S.TRANSL: Now I'm going to tell the story of Naparamaci of former times.

S.FORM: sua ni-pala-anal-a naparamaci ia, ʔuuna=kani manu nannakə.
S.PHON: sua nipaɾaanaɾa naparamatʂi ia ʔuunakani manu nannakə
S.FORM: sua niparaanara naparamaci ia, 'uunakani manu nannake.
S.PHON: sua nipa[r|ɾ]aana[r|ɾ]a napa[r|ɾ]amatʂi ia ʔuunakani manu nannake
S.TRANSL: As for the story of Naparamaci, there was a girl.

S.FORM: sua nannakə iisua ia, kanə ma-naasə makai na=cəpəŋ=kia ni-pita-nanala sua nannakə iisua.
S.PHON: sua nannakə iisua ia kanə manaasə makai naʦəpəŋkia nipitananaɾa sua nannakə iisua
S.FORM: sua nannake iisua ia, kane manaase makai nacepengkia nipitananara sua nannake iisua.
S.PHON: sua nannake iisua ia kane manaase makai naʦepeŋkia nipitanana[r|ɾ]a sua nannake iisua
S.TRANSL: As for that girl, she became an orphan like me.

S.FORM: maka-sua=kani sua nannakə iisua ia, ʔakia=kani maamia ma-ləəʔə ʔinia cau.
S.PHON: makasuakani sua nannakə iisua ia ʔakiakani maamia maɾəəʔə ʔinia ʦau
S.FORM: makasuakani sua nannake iisua ia, 'akiakani maamia maree'e 'inia cau.
S.PHON: makasuakani sua nannake iisua ia ʔakiakani maamia ma[r|ɾ]eeʔe ʔinia ʦau
S.TRANSL: And that girl being what she was, there was not even one person who cared for her.

S.FORM: ʔapacuʔ-ai nuu ʔuuna-ini kaən-a ia, avalaʔi kaʔaniman-a, kaʔan=kani maamia pirapa-ən=kiai mu-vua sua nannakə iisua.
S.PHON: ʔapaʦuʔai nuu ʔuunaini kaəna ia avaɾaʔi kaʔanimana kaʔankani maamia pirapaənkiai muvua sua nannakə iisua
S.FORM: 'apacu'ai nuu 'uunaini kaena ia, avara'i ka'animana, ka'ankani maamia pirapaenkiai muvua sua nannake iisua.
S.PHON: ʔapaʦuʔai nuu ʔuunaini kaena ia ava[r|ɾ]aʔi kaʔanimana kaʔankani maamia pi[r|ɾ]apaenkiai muvua sua nannake iisua
S.TRANSL: Even if they had food, whatever they would like to have, they would never share with the girl.

S.FORM: maka-sua=cu sua nannakə iisua ia, kanə ma-naasə ni-ma-ləmələmə sua nannakə iisua.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu sua nannakə iisua ia kanə manaasə nimaɾəməɾəmə sua nannakə iisua
S.FORM: makasuacu sua nannake iisua ia, kane manaase nimaremereme sua nannake iisua.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu sua nannake iisua ia kane manaase nima[r|ɾ]eme[r|ɾ]eme sua nannake iisua
S.TRANSL: And that girl being what she was, she could very well have God's blessings.

S.FORM: m-i-aranasə=cu ma-kasi m-ərə-ʔəəʔə maamia cucua, kaʔan kaʔaməc-ən cau s<um>a-nikusa.
S.PHON: miaranasəʦu makaʂi mərəʔəəʔə maamia ʦuʦua kaʔan kaʔaməʦən ʦau sumanikusa
S.FORM: miaranasecu makasi mere'ee'e maamia cucua, ka'an ka'amecen cau s<um>anikusa.
S.PHON: mia[r|ɾ]anaseʦu makaʂi me[r|ɾ]eʔeeʔe maamia ʦuʦua kaʔan kaʔameʦen ʦau sumanikusa
S.TRANSL: She was so miserable that she could only envy others. She did not even expect people to pay attention to her.

S.FORM: ara-tatia=cu sua nannakə iisua, mu-caanə=cu ʔaisi=cu tia=taka-cii-cini ti-kirim=kani sua na tia=camai-ini.
S.PHON: aratatiaʦu sua nannakə iisua muʦaanəʦu ʔaiʂiʦu tiatakatʂiitʂini tikirimkani sua na tiaʦamaiini
S.FORM: aratatiacu sua nannake iisua, mucaanecu 'aisicu tiatakaciicini tikirimkani sua na tiacamaiini.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]atatiaʦu sua nannake iisua muʦaaneʦu ʔaiʂiʦu tiatakatʂiitʂini tiki[r|ɾ]imkani sua na tiaʦamaiini
S.TRANSL: As the girl grew older, she would go by herself to find her own food.

S.FORM: mu-caanə=kani si mia-iisua ia, pu-cikura=kani sua cakəranə, naatia=kani l<um>a-liuʔu misa mu-caanə=kani sua nannakə iisua.
S.PHON: muʦaanəkani ʂi miaiisua ia putʂikurakani sua ʦakəranə naatiakani ɾumaɾiuʔu misa muʦaanəkani sua nannakə iisua
S.FORM: mucaanekani si miaiisua ia, pucikurakani sua cakerane, naatiakani r<um>ariu'u misa mucaanekani sua nannake iisua.
S.PHON: muʦaanekani ʂi miaiisua ia putʂiku[r|ɾ]akani sua ʦake[r|ɾ]ane naatiakani [r|ɾ]uma[r|ɾ]iuʔu misa muʦaanekani sua nannake iisua
S.TRANSL: She went—at that time the river was muddy. The girl went (there) to fish with a net, as she said.

S.FORM: um-avici sua sapuarə, tia=kani l<um>a-liuʔu.
S.PHON: umavitʂi sua sapuarə tiakani ɾumaɾiuʔu
S.FORM: umavici sua sapuare, tiakani r<um>ariu'u.
S.PHON: umavitʂi sua sapua[r|ɾ]e tiakani [r|ɾ]uma[r|ɾ]iuʔu
S.TRANSL: Bringing her fishnet along, she would go fishing with a net.

S.FORM: m-ala-kusa=kani cu-canumu sapuar-ini m-ari-takarə, ʔaisi=kani ta-sikar-a-ini taŋərə kaalu.
S.PHON: maɾakusakani ʦuʦanumu sapuarini maritakarə ʔaiʂikani taʂikaraini taŋərə kaaɾu
S.FORM: marakusakani cucanumu sapuarini maritakare, 'aisikani tasikaraini tangere kaaru.
S.PHON: ma[r|ɾ]akusakani ʦuʦanumu sapua[r|ɾ]ini ma[r|ɾ]itaka[r|ɾ]e ʔaiʂikani taʂika[r|ɾ]aini taŋe[r|ɾ]e kaa[r|ɾ]u
S.TRANSL: When she put her fishnet into the water and (then) brought it up, inside it there was a small piece of wood.

S.FORM: ala-i=kani ʔinia kaalu iisua t<um>aini na cu-canumu a-pa-ʔacunu.
S.PHON: aɾaikani ʔinia kaaɾu iisua tumaini na ʦuʦanumu apaʔaʦunu
S.FORM: araikani 'inia kaaru iisua t<um>aini na cucanumu apa'acunu.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]aikani ʔinia kaa[r|ɾ]u iisua tumaini na ʦuʦanumu apaʔaʦunu
S.TRANSL: She picked up the piece of wood, threw it into the water to let it drift away.

S.FORM: makasua=cu mu-laucu m-ala-ʔəna-ʔəna sapuar-ini, ʔaisi=kani ʔinia ta-sikar-a sapuar-ini ŋuai sua ni-mu-a-ʔuna sapuar-ini.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu muɾauʦu maɾaʔənaʔəna sapuarini ʔaiʂikani ʔinia taʂikara sapuarini ŋuai sua nimuaʔuna sapuarini
S.FORM: makasuacu muraucu mara'ena'ena sapuarini, 'aisikani 'inia tasikara sapuarini nguai sua nimua'una sapuarini.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu mu[r|ɾ]auʦu ma[r|ɾ]aʔenaʔena sapua[r|ɾ]ini ʔaiʂikani ʔinia taʂika[r|ɾ]a sapua[r|ɾ]ini ŋuai sua nimuaʔuna sapua[r|ɾ]ini
S.TRANSL: Thereupon, as she went down (the river) to put her net in again, inside her net was nothing but what had been in her net the first time.

S.FORM: ala-i=kani kaalu iisua pita-ʔəna-ʔəna pita-kusa na və-vəcəkai cu-canumu.
S.PHON: aɾaikani kaaɾu iisua pitaʔənaʔəna pitakusa na vəvəʦəkai ʦuʦanumu
S.FORM: araikani kaaru iisua pita'ena'ena pitakusa na vevecekai cucanumu.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]aikani kaa[r|ɾ]u iisua pitaʔenaʔena pitakusa na veveʦekai ʦuʦanumu
S.TRANSL: She took that piece of wood (out) and threw it once more into the water.

S.FORM: ma-kasi=kani a-ma-laucu m-ala-ʔəna-ʔəna m-ala-sapuarə ŋuai=kani sua kaalu ʔaisi p-ala-sapu-sapuar-a-in.
S.PHON: makaʂikani amaɾauʦu maɾaʔənaʔəna maɾasapuarə ŋuaikani sua kaaɾu ʔaiʂi paɾasapusapuarain
S.FORM: makasikani amaraucu mara'ena'ena marasapuare nguaikani sua kaaru 'aisi parasapusapuarain.
S.PHON: makaʂikani ama[r|ɾ]auʦu ma[r|ɾ]aʔenaʔena ma[r|ɾ]asapua[r|ɾ]e ŋuaikani sua kaa[r|ɾ]u ʔaiʂi pa[r|ɾ]asapusapua[r|ɾ]ain
S.TRANSL: She went down the river, put the net in again, (what she got) was still the piece of wood that had been in the net twice (before).

S.FORM: makasua=cu pasu-vuku-n maamia, "tia=avic-in tanasa tia=picinua=maku," misa=kani.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu pasuvukun maamia tiaavitʂin tanasa tiapitʂinuamaku misakani
S.FORM: makasuacu pasuvukun maamia, "tiaavicin tanasa tiapicinuamaku," misakani.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu pasuvukun maamia tiaavitʂin tanasa tiapitʂinuamaku misakani
S.TRANSL: Thereupon, she had no other choice but attached it to her belt. "It will be taken home to be my firewood," she said.

S.FORM: ala-i=kani ʔinia masu-vuku na ta-puru-vuku-a-ini ma-kasi tanasa.
S.PHON: aɾaikani ʔinia masuvuku na tapuruvukuaini makaʂi tanasa
S.FORM: araikani 'inia masuvuku na tapuruvukuaini makasi tanasa.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]aikani ʔinia masuvuku na tapu[r|ɾ]uvukuaini makaʂi tanasa
S.TRANSL: She picked it up, attached it to the belt around her waist and went home.

S.FORM: ma-ka-cəkəna tanasa mati-sapəsapə=kani sua ni-pasu-vuku=kiai picinua, tia=um-ala misa, mati-kiri-kirimi ʔakia=kani.
S.PHON: makaʦəkəna tanasa matisapəsapəkani sua nipasuvukukiai pitʂinua tiaumaɾa misa matikirikirimi ʔakiakani
S.FORM: makacekena tanasa matisapesapekani sua nipasuvukukiai picinua, tiaumara misa, matikirikirimi 'akiakani.
S.PHON: makaʦekena tanasa matisapesapekani sua nipasuvukukiai pitʂinua tiauma[r|ɾ]a misa matiki[r|ɾ]iki[r|ɾ]imi ʔakiakani
S.TRANSL: (When) she arrived home, she groped for the firewood that she had attached to the belt, but she could find nothing.

S.FORM: makasua=cu mia-ranau=cu ara-surumau=kani kaʔan ma-manəŋ cinəvəra-ini.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu miaranauʦu arasurumaukani kaʔan mamanəŋ tʂinəvəraini
S.FORM: makasuacu miaranaucu arasurumaukani ka'an mamaneng cineveraini.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu mia[r|ɾ]anauʦu a[r|ɾ]asu[r|ɾ]umaukani kaʔan mamaneŋ tʂineve[r|ɾ]aini
S.TRANSL: After a long time, her condition worsened (she became pregnant) without her knowing it.

S.FORM: makasua=cu mia-ranau, tia=kani=cu kaa-manu-manu=kiai, mu-caan=cu mu-kusa na tanasa kalavuŋ.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu miaranau tiakaniʦu kaamanumanukiai muʦaanʦu mukusa na tanasa kaɾavuŋ
S.FORM: makasuacu miaranau, tiakanicu kaamanumanukiai, mucaancu mukusa na tanasa karavung.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu mia[r|ɾ]anau tiakaniʦu kaamanumanukiai muʦaanʦu mukusa na tanasa ka[r|ɾ]avuŋ
S.TRANSL: After a long time, (when) her time to give birth, she went to the cattle pen.

S.FORM: mata-atəa ʔinia pusu-panaʔ-ai ʔinia sua manu-ini.
S.PHON: mataatəa ʔinia pusupanaʔai ʔinia sua manuini
S.FORM: mataatea 'inia pusupana'ai 'inia sua manuini.
S.PHON: mataatea ʔinia pusupanaʔai ʔinia sua manuini
S.TRANSL: She reached there, then she gave birth to her child.

S.FORM: makasua=cu m-i-aranasə, pakə-nanu mia-iisua ia, "ʔuuna cikia-ai kaʔaməcə lavini, pasəŋəsəŋə=cu ʔakia."
S.PHON: makasuaʦu miaranasə pakənanu miaiisua ia ʔuuna tʂikiaai kaʔaməʦə ɾavini pasəŋəsəŋəʦu ʔakia
S.FORM: makasuacu miaranase, pakenanu miaiisua ia, "'uuna cikiaai ka'amece ravini, pasengesengecu 'akia."
S.PHON: makasuaʦu mia[r|ɾ]anase pakenanu miaiisua ia ʔuuna tʂikiaai kaʔameʦe [r|ɾ]avini paseŋeseŋeʦu ʔakia
S.TRANSL: She was miserable. For at that time, "I cannot expect to have even a piece of dishcloth, not even a little something."

S.FORM: m-ətəa=kani sua ma-naasə na siʔan, ala-i=kani ʔinia, mu-pu-pucu ʔinia ka-manəŋ.
S.PHON: mətəakani sua manaasə na ʂiʔan aɾaikani ʔinia mupupuʦu ʔinia kamanəŋ
S.FORM: meteakani sua manaase na si'an, araikani 'inia, mupupucu 'inia kamaneng.
S.PHON: meteakani sua manaase na ʂiʔan a[r|ɾ]aikani ʔinia mupupuʦu ʔinia kamaneŋ
S.TRANSL: She found what was perhaps a piece of cloth potholder, took it and wrapped up the baby nice and secure.

S.FORM: makasua=cu ara-tatia=cu manu-ini iisua, kanə ma-naasə tavalaʔ-ən=cu=kiai um-arivi iimu ari-pa-piniŋ-in=cu=kiai.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu aratatiaʦu manuini iisua kanə manaasə tavaɾaʔənʦukiai umarivi iimu aripapiniŋinʦukiai
S.FORM: makasuacu aratatiacu manuini iisua, kane manaase tavara'encukiai umarivi iimu aripapiningincukiai.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu a[r|ɾ]atatiaʦu manuini iisua kane manaase tava[r|ɾ]aʔenʦukiai uma[r|ɾ]ivi iimu a[r|ɾ]ipapiniŋinʦukiai
S.TRANSL: As the baby grew older, it therefore could perhaps be carried in one's arms and taken outdoors.

S.FORM: ariv-ai=kani ʔinia m-avici pi-piniŋi, a-lakau=kani tapianaŋai.
S.PHON: arivaikani ʔinia mavitʂi pipiniŋi aɾakaukani tapianaŋai
S.FORM: arivaikani 'inia mavici pipiningi, arakaukani tapianangai.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]ivaikani ʔinia mavitʂi pipiniŋi a[r|ɾ]akaukani tapianaŋai
S.TRANSL: As (the baby) was carried in (her) arms and taken outside, a bird came flying over.

S.FORM: pakas-ai=kani ʔinia manu-ini, "cəʔəra-ən piai iisua," misa mati-saaʔə ramucu-ini.
S.PHON: pakasaikani ʔinia manuini ʦəʔəraən piai iisua misa matisaaʔə ramuʦuini
S.FORM: pakasaikani 'inia manuini, "ce'eraen piai iisua," misa matisaa'e ramucuini.
S.PHON: pakasaikani ʔinia manuini ʦeʔe[r|ɾ]aen piai iisua misa matisaaʔe [r|ɾ]amuʦuini
S.TRANSL: She talked to her baby, "Look! That birdie," and held its hand.

S.FORM: mia-kusa na tapianaŋai, "piai iisua" misa, mata-paliʔi=kani sua tapianaŋai.
S.PHON: miakusa na tapianaŋai piai iisua misa matapaɾiʔikani sua tapianaŋai
S.FORM: miakusa na tapianangai, "piai iisua" misa, matapari'ikani sua tapianangai.
S.PHON: miakusa na tapianaŋai piai iisua misa matapa[r|ɾ]iʔikani sua tapianaŋai
S.TRANSL: As (the baby pointed its finger) at the bird, saying "that birdie", the bird fell (from the sky).

S.FORM: makasua=cu ala-i=kani ʔinia tapianaŋai um-avici tanasa.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu aɾaikani ʔinia tapianaŋai umavitʂi tanasa
S.FORM: makasuacu araikani 'inia tapianangai umavici tanasa.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu a[r|ɾ]aikani ʔinia tapianaŋai umavitʂi tanasa
S.TRANSL: Thereupon, she took the bird and brought it home.

S.FORM: makasua=cu ara-tatia=kani=cu sua manu-ini ma-naasə tavalaʔə=cu mu-caca-canə iimu tavalaʔə=cu mati-mua-muarə. ka-manəŋ vuuru sua makai ta-tiʔiŋ-ai mati-mua-muarə.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu aratatiakaniʦu sua manuini manaasə tavaɾaʔəʦu muʦaʦaʦanə iimu tavaɾaʔəʦu matimuamuarə kamanəŋ vuuru sua makai tatiʔiŋai matimuamuarə
S.FORM: makasuacu aratatiakanicu sua manuini manaase tavara'ecu mucacacane iimu tavara'ecu matimuamuare. kamaneng vuuru sua makai tati'ingai matimuamuare.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu a[r|ɾ]atatiakaniʦu sua manuini manaase tava[r|ɾ]aʔeʦu muʦaʦaʦane iimu tava[r|ɾ]aʔeʦu matimuamua[r|ɾ]e kamaneŋ vuu[r|ɾ]u sua makai tatiʔiŋai matimuamua[r|ɾ]e
S.TRANSL: As her child grew older, it therefore could perhaps walk around and play at making bows, the way little children play.

S.FORM: makasua=cu ka-manəŋ vuuru.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu kamanəŋ vuuru
S.FORM: makasuacu kamaneng vuuru.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu kamaneŋ vuu[r|ɾ]u
S.TRANSL: Thereupon, (the child) made bows.

S.FORM: makasua=cu sua manu iisua ia, panan miana ia, ʔapacuʔ-ai sua na=mu-liuŋ ia, kacaua=pa mara-kəra-kərapə.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu sua manu iisua ia panan miana ia ʔapaʦuʔai sua namuɾiuŋ ia kaʦauapa marakərakərapə
S.FORM: makasuacu sua manu iisua ia, panan miana ia, 'apacu'ai sua namuriung ia, kacauapa marakerakerape.
S.PHON: makasuaʦu sua manu iisua ia panan miana ia ʔapaʦuʔai sua namu[r|ɾ]iuŋ ia kaʦauapa ma[r|ɾ]ake[r|ɾ]ake[r|ɾ]ape
S.TRANSL: Thereupon, the child--because it was long time ago, even in the vicinity (of where people live), there were still many animals around.

S.FORM: cəʔəra-i=kani manu-ini sua ma-naasə anuka vavulu iacuʔu-ai=kani ʔinia sua vuuru-ini ma-naasə ʔu-rupaca rupacə.
S.PHON: ʦəʔəraikani manuini sua manaasə anuka vavuɾu iaʦuʔuaikani ʔinia sua vuuruini manaasə ʔurupaʦa rupaʦə
S.FORM: ce'eraikani manuini sua manaase anuka vavuru iacu'uaikani 'inia sua vuuruini manaase 'urupaca rupace.
S.PHON: ʦeʔe[r|ɾ]aikani manuini sua manaase anuka vavu[r|ɾ]u iaʦuʔuaikani ʔinia sua vuu[r|ɾ]uini manaase ʔu[r|ɾ]upaʦa [r|ɾ]upaʦe
S.TRANSL: As her son saw what was perhaps the footprints of a wild pig, he aimed his bow at them, using an arrow.

S.FORM: surumau=kani sua vavulu um-uliʔi tim-cala.
S.PHON: surumaukani sua vavuɾu umuɾiʔi timʦaɾa
S.FORM: surumaukani sua vavuru umuri'i timcara.
S.PHON: su[r|ɾ]umaukani sua vavu[r|ɾ]u umu[r|ɾ]iʔi timʦa[r|ɾ]a
S.TRANSL: Suddenly the wild pig squealed from above.

S.FORM: t<um>imana=kani sua cau "ʔaisi makananu sua vavulu um-a-uliʔi?" misa=kani.
